title: No for Some, Yes for Others: Persona Prompts and Other Sources of False Refusal in Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The study measured the rate of 'false refusals' (i.e., refusing safe requests) from Large Language Models when prompted with various sociodemographic personas, including religious identities. This was tested across three NLP classification tasks: Natural Language Inference, politeness classification, and offensiveness classification.
findings: Certain religious personas led to significantly higher false refusal rates. Specifically, prompts including 'Muslim' and 'Jewish' personas elicited higher refusals. In contrast, 'Christian' and 'Atheist' personas were among those with the lowest refusal rates. This suggests underlying biases in the models' safety mechanisms related to specific religious groups.
